newsitem.title: CHINA: China Moslem region executes bomber.
newsitem.headline: China Moslem region executes bomber.

text.p: Authorities in China's restive northwestern region of Xinjiang have executed a Moslem for bombing a military jeep last year, a court official said on Monday.

Maimaiti Wubulihasimu, 28, a self-taught expert on the Koran, was executed on April 28 after the Xinjiang Higher People's Court upheld the death sentence handed down by a lower court, the official said.
"Execute one as a warning to a hundred," the Xinjiang Legal Daily said in an edition seen in Beijing on Monday.
Co-defendant Maimaiti Musilimu, 25, a student of the Koran, was given a suspended death sentence, the official said. Suspended death sentences are usually commuted to life imprisonment.

Both men, members of the ethnic Uighur minority, were found guilty of blowing up a military jeep with a home-made bomb in the regional capital, Urumqi, in February, 1996, the official said. He declined to say what the motive of the bombers was.

Further bombings occurred in Xinjiang this year. On February 25, bombs planted on three buses blew up within minutes of each other in Urumqi in an apparently coordinated attack that coincided with funeral rites in Beijing for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
Exiled Uighur separatists have claimed responsibility for that attack. Turkish-speaking Uighurs want to set up an independent East Turkestan in Xinjiang.
The Xinjiang Legal Daily said the execution served as a "warning to criminal elements who (resort to) extreme violence to attempt to split the motherland...sabotage social stability."
The defendants were also convicted of armed robbery and murdering one of their victims, the court official said. He declined to provide further details.

On Sunday, Abdulahat Abdurixit, chairman of the Xinjiang regional government, said separatist activities were doomed to failure, Chinese regional television from Xinjiang, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corp, reported.
"Separatism and illegal religious activities carried out by ethnic separatists do not enjoy popular support, and are doomed to failure," Abdurixit said in an interview with French reporters.
"Ethnic separatists pursuing separatism and carrying out activities of terrorism and sabotage do not represent any ethnic group, and their activities are not a question of religion.

"These activities of sabotage jeopardise the interests of the state and people of all ethnic groups. For this reason, people of all ethnic groups do not approve of them, and they are doomed to failure," he said, quoted by the television.
Xinjiang has launched an education campaign in government offices, using propaganda films and books to spread the message of ethnic unity and prevent separatist violence.
Last month, Chinese authorities executed three rioters and opened fire on a mob trying to rescue the death-row convicts.
Riots in Yining in February this year had began as a demonstration for Xinjiang independence and turned violent, leaving nine people dead and 198 injured.
Xinjiang has been shaken since last year by increasingly frequent bombings as well as assassination attempts on officials and Moslem leaders seen as favouring Beijing.
Xinjiang borders Afghanistan, Pakistan and three mostly Moslem Central Asian states.
